dedupe_keys.name: global iron and steel tracker gist

description: The Global Iron and Steel Tracker from Global Energy Monitor lists crude iron and steel plants worldwide with a capacity of 500,000 tonnes per year or more of crude iron or steel, including plants proposed or under construction since 2017 and plants retired or mothballed since 2020. On 26 September 2026 it counted 1,293 plants in 91 countries and areas, more than 1,000 owners and 3.7 billion tonnes of annual crude steel capacity. Plants are broken into units by production route: blast furnace and basic oxygen furnace, open hearth furnace, electric arc furnace charged with scrap, pig iron or direct reduced iron, and direct reduction. Each plant has location, ownership, status, capacities by process and a GEM.wiki page with sources. The latest release was March 2026, with a limited quarterly update in June 2026; data are updated annually. Access is a free map, dashboard and summary tables, and a spreadsheet after a download request form, under CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: smaller plants below the threshold are not included, and historic capacity of retired units is only partly kept. For simulation it is an asset inventory of steel plants for supply-chain, hazard exposure and decarbonisation studies of heavy industry and its power and gas demand. Related catalogue records include the Global Iron Ore Mines Tracker, the SFI GeoAsset databases and Climate TRACE.
